The '''2018 [[Eliteserien]]''' was the 74th completed season of top-tier [[Association football|football]] in [[Norway]]. This was second season of Eliteserien as rebranding from Tippeligaen.

The season began on 11 March and ended 24 November 2018, not including play-off matches.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hovedterminliste menn 2018 |url=https://www.fotball.no/contentassets/2ff93e9eef834ce29aab48f7d908e4c7/hovedterminliste-menn-2018.pdf |website=fotball.no}}</ref> Fixtures for the 2018 season were announced on 19 December 2017.<ref>{{cite web|title= Terminlisten er klar: Slik spilles Eliteserien 2018|url=https://www.aftenposten.no/100Sport/fotball/Terminlisten-er-klar-Slik-spilles-Eliteserien-2018-247233b.html
|website=aftenposten.no|publisher=Aftenposten|access-date=8 June 2018|language=no|date=19 December 2017}}</ref> [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] were the defending champions, while [[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]], [[IK Start|Start]] and [[Ranheim Fotball|Ranheim]] entered as the promoted teams from the [[2017 1. divisjon]].

Rosenborg won their fourth consecutive title, their 26th top-flight title overall, with one match to spare following a 1–0 away win against [[IK Start|Start]] on 11 November 2018.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nrk.no/sport/rosenborg-vant-eliteserien_-_-de-har-ikke-vaert-gode_-men-gode-nok-1.14288714 |title=Rosenborg vant Eliteserien: – Det har vært et vanvittig turbulent år |language=no |website=[[NRK]] Sport |publisher=NRK |date=11 November 2018 |access-date=7 May 2019}}</ref>

==Overview==
===Summary===
[[SK Brann|Brann]] started the season well and won eight of their nine opening games. They lost their first match 0–4 against [[Molde FK|Molde]] in the 15th round. [[Rosenborg BK|Rosenborg]] started the season poorly with no win in the first three games, but managed to tighten the gap to [[SK Brann|Brann]]. Head coach [[Kåre Ingebrigtsen]] was sacked on 19 July<ref name="Ingebrigtsen sacked">{{Cite news |title=Styrelederen om sparkingen av Ingebrigtsen: – Ubehagelig og tøft |language=no|url=https://www.nrk.no/sport/ingebrigtsen-ferdig-i-rosenborg-1.14132983 |publisher=NRK |date=19 July 2018 |access-date=20 July 2018}}</ref> although Rosenborg was placed second in the league, two points behind Brann at the time. 

On 11 November, Rosenborg were confirmed as Eliteserien champions following their 1–0 away win against [[IK Start|Start]] in the 29th round. They won their fourth consecutive title and 26th top-flight title overall. Molde won eight of their final nine games and finished in second place, five points behind Rosenborg.

[[Sandefjord Fotball|Sandefjord]] were the first team to be relegated to the 1. divisjon when they drew 1–1 against [[Sarpsborg 08 FF|Sarpsborg 08]] in their penultimate game. Before the 30th and final round, five teams were in risk of either relegation or relegation play-offs. Start lost 1–3 away to [[FK Haugesund|Haugesund]] and was relegated as the second team from bottom. [[Stabæk Fotball|Stabæk]] drew 2–2 against [[Strømsgodset Toppfotball|Strømsgodset]] after a goal by Strømsgodset's [[Mustafa Abdellaoue]] in the last minute of the game. That goal made sure Strømsgodset retained their spot in the next season's Eliteserien, while Stabæk were forced to play relegation play-offs.<ref>{{Cite news |title=Strømsgodset reddet Eliteserie-kontrakten på overtid – sendte Stabæk til kvalik |language=no|url=https://www.eurosport.no/fotball/eliteserien/2018/stromsgodset-reddet-eliteserie-kontrakten-pa-overtid-sendte-stabaek-til-kvalik_sto7024927/story.shtml |publisher=Eurosport |work=eurosport.no |date=24 November 2018 |access-date=27 November 2018}}</ref> Stabæk won the play-offs against [[Aalesunds FK|Aalesund]] 2–1 on aggregate and retained their spot in Eliteserien.

==Teams==
Sixteen teams competed in the league – the top thirteen teams from the previous season, and three teams promoted from [[2017 1. divisjon|1. divisjon]]. The promoted teams were [[FK Bodø/Glimt|Bodø/Glimt]], [[IK Start|Start]] (both returning to the top flight after a season's absence) and [[Ranheim Fotball|Ranheim]] (returned to the top flight after an absence of sixty-one years). They replaced [[Sogndal Fotball|Sogndal]], [[Aalesunds FK|Aalesund]] and [[Viking FK|Viking]] ending their top flight spells of two, eleven and twenty-nine years respectively.

==Relegation play-offs==
{{Main|2018 Eliteserien promotion/relegation play-offs}}
The 14th-placed team, Stabæk takes part in a two-legged play-off against Aalesund, the winners of the [[2018 1. divisjon#Promotion play-offs|1. divisjon promotion play-offs]], to decide who will play in the [[2019 Eliteserien]].
{{football box
